occurrences.extract: We seek approval for Halden Group to invest up to EUR 480 million of equity in the acquisition of Helvetia Precision Components AG ("HPC" or "the Company"), a Zurich-headquartered manufacturer of high-precision machined components for the medical devices, aerospace, and semiconductor end markets. The transaction values HPC at an enterprise value of EUR 1.15 billion, representing 11.2x trailing twelve months EBITDA of EUR 103 million. Halden Group would acquire a 78% controlling stake from the founding Schiller family, with the remainder retained by management. The seller is being advised by Lincoln International.

HPC has grown revenue from EUR 312 million in 2020 to EUR 587 million in 2024, a compound annual growth rate of 17.1%. EBITDA over the same period has expanded from EUR 48 million to EUR 103 million, with margins improving from 15.4% to 17.5%. Growth has been split roughly evenly between organic share gains and the contribution from the Indianapolis acquisition. Free cash flow conversion has averaged 71% across the period.

Third, there is a clear margin expansion path. HPC's current EBITDA margin of 17.5% trails best-in-class peers (Burckhardt Compression at 19.8%, VAT Group at 31.2% — though VAT operates in a different segment) and our diligence has identified a coherent set of operational levers we believe can deliver 300 to 400 basis points of margin uplift over five years. The principal levers are: footprint consolidation in Switzerland (closing the Winterthur facility and absorbing volumes into Olten), procurement consolidation across the now-fragmented supplier base inherited from the Indianapolis acquisition, and a programme of automation investment in the Brno facility.

The semiconductor exposure introduces cyclicality that the medical and aerospace segments do not. In the 2023 downcycle, HPC's semiconductor revenue declined by 28% year-on-year, though overall Company revenue still grew due to offsetting strength in the other segments. We are comfortable with this exposure given (a) the structural growth in EUV, and (b) HPC's flexible cost base, which allowed the Company to maintain EBITDA margins above 15% throughout the 2023 downturn.

EBITDA margin expansion from 17.5% to 21.0% over the hold period, delivering EBITDA of approximately EUR 190 million by 2029. The margin lift is sourced from the footprint consolidation programme (approximately 120 bps), procurement initiatives (approximately 80 bps), automation investment in Brno (approximately 60 bps), and operating leverage on incremental revenue (approximately 60 bps).

Multiple expansion is not assumed in the base case. We underwrite an exit at 11.0x EBITDA, marginally below the entry multiple, reflecting prudence regarding sector multiples five years forward. In our upside case, multiple expansion to 12.5x reflects the higher-margin, more diversified, larger-scale platform we expect HPC to become.

The transaction will be funded with EUR 480 million of equity from Halden Group, EUR 130 million of equity from co-investors (currently anticipated to include two existing LP relationships), and EUR 540 million of senior and second-lien debt. Total leverage at close is approximately 5.2x trailing EBITDA, which we view as appropriate given the Company's cash generation profile and recession-resilient end-market mix. Goldman Sachs and Credit Suisse have provided fully underwritten commitments.

We have already identified five actionable targets in the EUR 30–80 million enterprise value range that would be accretive on both growth and margin grounds. The base case returns of 2.4x / 19% are in line with our private equity portfolio benchmarks, and we see meaningful upside optionality from M&A and end-market acceleration. The risks are well-understood and manageable. We recommend approval.

Switching costs for medical device OEMs are substantial — qualification of a new supplier typically takes 18 to 24 months and involves clinical trial impact assessments. Andreas Schiller has committed to remain on the board for the first three years post-close and will rollover approximately 8% of his proceeds into the transaction.

We will recruit a Chief Commercial Officer post-close — a role HPC has historically not had — to coordinate the global customer interface across the three end markets. We have already identified a strong candidate currently working in a senior commercial role at GF Machining Solutions.

The Schiller family will retain a 15% economic interest. Management will hold the remaining 7%. We have negotiated standard tag-along and drag-along rights, and a clear governance framework giving Halden Group majority board representation (3 of 5 seats).

occurrences.extract: We seek approval for Halden Group to invest up to EUR 480 million of equity in the acquisition of Helvetia Precision Components AG ("HPC" or "the Company"), a Zurich-headquartered manufacturer of high-precision machined components for the medical devices, aerospace, and semiconductor end markets. The transaction values HPC at an enterprise value of EUR 1.15 billion, representing 11.2x trailing twelve months EBITDA of EUR 103 million. Halden Group would acquire a 78% controlling stake from the founding Schiller family, with the remainder retained by management. The seller is being advised by Lincoln International.

HPC was founded in 1962 by Werner Schiller in Winterthur. The Company manufactures complex precision components — typically machined to tolerances of 5 microns or tighter — for applications where failure is not an option. Roughly 48% of revenue is generated from medical device customers, primarily orthopaedic implants and surgical instruments. A further 32% comes from aerospace, split between civil aviation engine components and defence applications. The remaining 20% serves semiconductor capital equipment manufacturers, where HPC supplies critical components used in wafer fabrication tools.

The Company operates four manufacturing facilities: a headquarters site in Winterthur (Switzerland), a larger production facility in Olten (Switzerland), a US operation in Indianapolis acquired in 2018, and a smaller Czech facility in Brno established in 2021 to serve European aerospace customers at lower cost. Total headcount stands at 1,420 employees, of whom approximately 240 are based outside Switzerland.

First, the Company occupies an enviable competitive position. In its core medical implants vertical, HPC is one of three qualified suppliers globally for hip and knee replacement components meeting both FDA Class II and EU MDR requirements at scale. Switching costs for medical device OEMs are substantial — qualification of a new supplier typically takes 18 to 24 months and involves clinical trial impact assessments. As a result, customer relationships are durable: HPC's top 10 customers have been with the Company for an average of 14 years, and revenue retention from these accounts has been 102% over the past five years.

The semiconductor exposure introduces cyclicality that the medical and aerospace segments do not. In the 2023 downcycle, HPC's semiconductor revenue declined by 28% year-on-year, though overall Company revenue still grew due to offsetting strength in the other segments. We are comfortable with this exposure given (a) the structural growth in EUV, and (b) HPC's flexible cost base, which allowed the Company to maintain EBITDA margins above 15% throughout the 2023 downturn.

Customer concentration is a watch item. HPC's largest customer, a global orthopaedic implants manufacturer, accounted for 18% of revenue in 2024. While the relationship is multi-decade and contractually backed by long-term supply agreements, any meaningful disruption to this account would materially impact Company performance.

Founder transition risk is moderate. Andreas Schiller, son of the founder, has served as CEO for 17 years and will step back to the board post-close. The Company has identified an internal successor — Petra Köhler, currently COO — who is well-regarded by the management team and customers. We have completed extensive reference checks. Andreas Schiller has committed to remain on the board for the first three years post-close and will rollover approximately 8% of his proceeds into the transaction.

The broader management team is mature, but we have identified the procurement function as under-resourced relative to the Company's scale and complexity. A Chief Procurement Officer will be recruited in year one, with a mandate to deliver the EUR 8–12 million of annualised procurement savings identified in diligence.

The transaction will be funded with EUR 480 million of equity from Halden Group, EUR 130 million of equity from co-investors (currently anticipated to include two existing LP relationships), and EUR 540 million of senior and second-lien debt. Total leverage at close is approximately 5.2x trailing EBITDA, which we view as appropriate given the Company's cash generation profile and recession-resilient end-market mix. Goldman Sachs and Credit Suisse have provided fully underwritten commitments.

Diligence has been thorough. We engaged Bain & Company on commercial diligence (six weeks, completed late February), Deloitte on financial and tax diligence, Kirkland & Ellis on legal, and ERM on ESG and environmental diligence. The Bain report — circulated separately — confirms our market positioning thesis and identifies an additional EUR 14 million of revenue synergies from cross-selling between segments that we have not underwritten in the base case.

occurrences.extract: INVESTMENT MEMORANDUM — STRICTLY CONFIDENTIAL
To:        Global Investment Committee
From:      European Industrials Team — Stefan Brunner (Partner), Lena Hofmann (Member of Management), Tobias Reichmann (Senior Vice President)
Date:      14 March 2025
Subject:   Project Alpine — Proposed acquisition of Helvetia Precision Components AG
RECOMMENDATION

We seek approval for Halden Group to invest up to EUR 480 million of equity in the acquisition of Helvetia Precision Components AG ("HPC" or "the Company"), a Zurich-headquartered manufacturer of high-precision machined components for the medical devices, aerospace, and semiconductor end markets. The transaction values HPC at an enterprise value of EUR 1.15 billion, representing 11.2x trailing twelve months EBITDA of EUR 103 million. Halden Group would acquire a 78% controlling stake from the founding Schiller family, with the remainder retained by management. The seller is being advised by Lincoln International.

HPC was founded in 1962 by Werner Schiller in Winterthur. The Company manufactures complex precision components — typically machined to tolerances of 5 microns or tighter — for applications where failure is not an option. Roughly 48% of revenue is generated from medical device customers, primarily orthopaedic implants and surgical instruments. A further 32% comes from aerospace, split between civil aviation engine components and defence applications. The remaining 20% serves semiconductor capital equipment manufacturers, where HPC supplies critical components used in wafer fabrication tools.

The Company operates four manufacturing facilities: a headquarters site in Winterthur (Switzerland), a larger production facility in Olten (Switzerland), a US operation in Indianapolis acquired in 2018, and a smaller Czech facility in Brno established in 2021 to serve European aerospace customers at lower cost. Total headcount stands at 1,420 employees, of whom approximately 240 are based outside Switzerland.

HPC has grown revenue from EUR 312 million in 2020 to EUR 587 million in 2024, a compound annual growth rate of 17.1%. EBITDA over the same period has expanded from EUR 48 million to EUR 103 million, with margins improving from 15.4% to 17.5%. Growth has been split roughly evenly between organic share gains and the contribution from the Indianapolis acquisition. Free cash flow conversion has averaged 71% across the period.
INVESTMENT THESIS

First, the Company occupies an enviable competitive position. In its core medical implants vertical, HPC is one of three qualified suppliers globally for hip and knee replacement components meeting both FDA Class II and EU MDR requirements at scale. Switching costs for medical device OEMs are substantial — qualification of a new supplier typically takes 18 to 24 months and involves clinical trial impact assessments. As a result, customer relationships are durable: HPC's top 10 customers have been with the Company for an average of 14 years, and revenue retention from these accounts has been 102% over the past five years.

Second, the end markets HPC serves are structurally attractive. The orthopaedic implants market is forecast to grow at 5–6% annually through 2030, driven by ageing demographics in Europe and the United States. Aerospace component demand is recovering strongly post-COVID, with Airbus and Boeing collectively targeting build-rate increases of approximately 40% over the next five years. Semiconductor capital equipment demand is more cyclical, but HPC's exposure is weighted toward EUV-related components, where structural demand growth is robust.

Third, there is a clear margin expansion path. HPC's current EBITDA margin of 17.5% trails best-in-class peers (Burckhardt Compression at 19.8%, VAT Group at 31.2% — though VAT operates in a different segment) and our diligence has identified a coherent set of operational levers we believe can deliver 300 to 400 basis points of margin uplift over five years. The principal levers are: footprint consolidation in Switzerland (closing the Winterthur facility and absorbing volumes into Olten), procurement consolidation across the now-fragmented supplier base inherited from the Indianapolis acquisition, and a programme of automation investment in the Brno facility.

Fourth, we see meaningful M&A opportunity. The European precision machining sector remains highly fragmented, with the top 10 players accounting for less than 30% of the market. We have already identified five actionable targets in the EUR 30–80 million enterprise value range that would be accretive on both growth and margin grounds. The founding family has historically been reluctant to pursue M&A; under our ownership we expect to complete two to three add-on acquisitions over the holding period.

The semiconductor exposure introduces cyclicality that the medical and aerospace segments do not. In the 2023 downcycle, HPC's semiconductor revenue declined by 28% year-on-year, though overall Company revenue still grew due to offsetting strength in the other segments. We are comfortable with this exposure given (a) the structural growth in EUV, and (b) HPC's flexible cost base, which allowed the Company to maintain EBITDA margins above 15% throughout the 2023 downturn.

Customer concentration is a watch item. HPC's largest customer, a global orthopaedic implants manufacturer, accounted for 18% of revenue in 2024. While the relationship is multi-decade and contractually backed by long-term supply agreements, any meaningful disruption to this account would materially impact Company performance.

Foreign exchange exposure is significant. Approximately 55% of revenue is denominated in EUR, 30% in USD, and the remainder in CHF and other currencies. Cost base is more heavily CHF-weighted given the Swiss manufacturing footprint. CHF strength against EUR over the past three years has cost HPC roughly 180 basis points of cumulative margin. We expect to hedge transaction exposure systematically post-close and have factored a normalised CHF/EUR rate of 0.98 into our base case.

Founder transition risk is moderate. Andreas Schiller, son of the founder, has served as CEO for 17 years and will step back to the board post-close. The Company has identified an internal successor — Petra Köhler, currently COO — who is well-regarded by the management team and customers. We have completed extensive reference checks. Andreas Schiller has committed to remain on the board for the first three years post-close and will rollover approximately 8% of his proceeds into the transaction.

Revenue growth of 9% CAGR, taking 2024 revenue of EUR 587 million to approximately EUR 905 million by 2029. This growth is composed of: 5% organic growth in line with end-market expansion, 2% from share gain in medical implants, and 2% from contemplated M&A.

EBITDA margin expansion from 17.5% to 21.0% over the hold period, delivering EBITDA of approximately EUR 190 million by 2029. The margin lift is sourced from the footprint consolidation programme (approximately 120 bps), procurement initiatives (approximately 80 bps), automation investment in Brno (approximately 60 bps), and operating leverage on incremental revenue (approximately 60 bps).

Multiple expansion is not assumed in the base case. We underwrite an exit at 11.0x EBITDA, marginally below the entry multiple, reflecting prudence regarding sector multiples five years forward. In our upside case, multiple expansion to 12.5x reflects the higher-margin, more diversified, larger-scale platform we expect HPC to become.

The base case generates a 2.4x gross MOIC and a 19% gross IRR. The upside case generates 3.1x gross MOIC and 24% gross IRR. The downside case — in which margin expansion delivers only 150 bps and revenue growth is held at 5% — generates 1.7x gross MOIC and 11% gross IRR.
MANAGEMENT AND ORGANISATION

Petra Köhler, age 49, will become CEO upon close. She joined HPC in 2009 from Sulzer, where she ran the rotating equipment business. She has held the COO role at HPC since 2018 and is credited internally with the success of the Indianapolis integration. The base case returns of 2.4x / 19% are in line with our private equity portfolio benchmarks, and we see meaningful upside optionality from M&A and end-market acceleration. occurrences.extract: INVESTMENT MEMORANDUM — STRICTLY CONFIDENTIAL
To:        Global Investment Committee
From:      European Industrials Team — Stefan Brunner (Partner), Lena Hofmann (Member of Management), Tobias Reichmann (Senior Vice President)
Date:      14 March 2025
Subject:   Project Alpine — Proposed acquisition of Helvetia Precision Components AG
RECOMMENDATION

We seek approval for Halden Group to invest up to EUR 480 million of equity in the acquisition of Helvetia Precision Components AG ("HPC" or "the Company"), a Zurich-headquartered manufacturer of high-precision machined components for the medical devices, aerospace, and semiconductor end markets. The transaction values HPC at an enterprise value of EUR 1.15 billion, representing 11.2x trailing twelve months EBITDA of EUR 103 million. Halden Group would acquire a 78% controlling stake from the founding Schiller family, with the remainder retained by management. The seller is being advised by Lincoln International.

HPC was founded in 1962 by Werner Schiller in Winterthur. The Company manufactures complex precision components — typically machined to tolerances of 5 microns or tighter — for applications where failure is not an option. Roughly 48% of revenue is generated from medical device customers, primarily orthopaedic implants and surgical instruments. A further 32% comes from aerospace, split between civil aviation engine components and defence applications. The remaining 20% serves semiconductor capital equipment manufacturers, where HPC supplies critical components used in wafer fabrication tools.

The Company operates four manufacturing facilities: a headquarters site in Winterthur (Switzerland), a larger production facility in Olten (Switzerland), a US operation in Indianapolis acquired in 2018, and a smaller Czech facility in Brno established in 2021 to serve European aerospace customers at lower cost. Total headcount stands at 1,420 employees, of whom approximately 240 are based outside Switzerland.

HPC has grown revenue from EUR 312 million in 2020 to EUR 587 million in 2024, a compound annual growth rate of 17.1%. EBITDA over the same period has expanded from EUR 48 million to EUR 103 million, with margins improving from 15.4% to 17.5%. Growth has been split roughly evenly between organic share gains and the contribution from the Indianapolis acquisition. Free cash flow conversion has averaged 71% across the period.
We are attracted to HPC for four reasons.

First, the Company occupies an enviable competitive position. In its core medical implants vertical, HPC is one of three qualified suppliers globally for hip and knee replacement components meeting both FDA Class II and EU MDR requirements at scale. Switching costs for medical device OEMs are substantial — qualification of a new supplier typically takes 18 to 24 months and involves clinical trial impact assessments. As a result, customer relationships are durable: HPC's top 10 customers have been with the Company for an average of 14 years, and revenue retention from these accounts has been 102% over the past five years.

Second, the end markets HPC serves are structurally attractive. The orthopaedic implants market is forecast to grow at 5–6% annually through 2030, driven by ageing demographics in Europe and the United States. Aerospace component demand is recovering strongly post-COVID, with Airbus and Boeing collectively targeting build-rate increases of approximately 40% over the next five years. Semiconductor capital equipment demand is more cyclical, but HPC's exposure is weighted toward EUV-related components, where structural demand growth is robust.

Third, there is a clear margin expansion path. HPC's current EBITDA margin of 17.5% trails best-in-class peers (Burckhardt Compression at 19.8%, VAT Group at 31.2% — though VAT operates in a different segment) and our diligence has identified a coherent set of operational levers we believe can deliver 300 to 400 basis points of margin uplift over five years. The principal levers are: footprint consolidation in Switzerland (closing the Winterthur facility and absorbing volumes into Olten), procurement consolidation across the now-fragmented supplier base inherited from the Indianapolis acquisition, and a programme of automation investment in the Brno facility.

Fourth, we see meaningful M&A opportunity. The European precision machining sector remains highly fragmented, with the top 10 players accounting for less than 30% of the market. We have already identified five actionable targets in the EUR 30–80 million enterprise value range that would be accretive on both growth and margin grounds. The founding family has historically been reluctant to pursue M&A; under our ownership we expect to complete two to three add-on acquisitions over the holding period.
We have identified four principal risks.

The semiconductor exposure introduces cyclicality that the medical and aerospace segments do not. In the 2023 downcycle, HPC's semiconductor revenue declined by 28% year-on-year, though overall Company revenue still grew due to offsetting strength in the other segments. We are comfortable with this exposure given (a) the structural growth in EUV, and (b) HPC's flexible cost base, which allowed the Company to maintain EBITDA margins above 15% throughout the 2023 downturn.

Customer concentration is a watch item. HPC's largest customer, a global orthopaedic implants manufacturer, accounted for 18% of revenue in 2024. While the relationship is multi-decade and contractually backed by long-term supply agreements, any meaningful disruption to this account would materially impact Company performance.

Foreign exchange exposure is significant. Approximately 55% of revenue is denominated in EUR, 30% in USD, and the remainder in CHF and other currencies. Cost base is more heavily CHF-weighted given the Swiss manufacturing footprint. CHF strength against EUR over the past three years has cost HPC roughly 180 basis points of cumulative margin. We expect to hedge transaction exposure systematically post-close and have factored a normalised CHF/EUR rate of 0.98 into our base case.

Founder transition risk is moderate. Andreas Schiller, son of the founder, has served as CEO for 17 years and will step back to the board post-close. The Company has identified an internal successor — Petra Köhler, currently COO — who is well-regarded by the management team and customers. We have completed extensive reference checks. Andreas Schiller has committed to remain on the board for the first three years post-close and will rollover approximately 8% of his proceeds into the transaction.
VALUE CREATION PLAN
Our base case underwrites a five-year hold with the following value drivers.

Revenue growth of 9% CAGR, taking 2024 revenue of EUR 587 million to approximately EUR 905 million by 2029. This growth is composed of: 5% organic growth in line with end-market expansion, 2% from share gain in medical implants, and 2% from contemplated M&A.

EBITDA margin expansion from 17.5% to 21.0% over the hold period, delivering EBITDA of approximately EUR 190 million by 2029. The margin lift is sourced from the footprint consolidation programme (approximately 120 bps), procurement initiatives (approximately 80 bps), automation investment in Brno (approximately 60 bps), and operating leverage on incremental revenue (approximately 60 bps).

Multiple expansion is not assumed in the base case. We underwrite an exit at 11.0x EBITDA, marginally below the entry multiple, reflecting prudence regarding sector multiples five years forward. In our upside case, multiple expansion to 12.5x reflects the higher-margin, more diversified, larger-scale platform we expect HPC to become.

The base case generates a 2.4x gross MOIC and a 19% gross IRR. The upside case generates 3.1x gross MOIC and 24% gross IRR. The downside case — in which margin expansion delivers only 150 bps and revenue growth is held at 5% — generates 1.7x gross MOIC and 11% gross IRR.
MANAGEMENT AND ORGANISATION

Petra Köhler, age 49, will become CEO upon close. She joined HPC in 2009 from Sulzer, where she ran the rotating equipment business. She has held the COO role at HPC since 2018 and is credited internally with the success of the Indianapolis integration. Reference checks across customers, suppliers, and former colleagues have been uniformly positive.

The CFO, Markus Zehnder, has been with HPC for 11 years and is well-regarded. We see no need to change this role. We will recruit a Chief Commercial Officer post-close — a role HPC has historically not had — to coordinate the global customer interface across the three end markets. We have already identified a strong candidate currently working in a senior commercial role at GF Machining Solutions.

The broader management team is mature, but we have identified the procurement function as under-resourced relative to the Company's scale and complexity. A Chief Procurement Officer will be recruited in year one, with a mandate to deliver the EUR 8–12 million of annualised procurement savings identified in diligence.
TRANSACTION STRUCTURE

The transaction will be funded with EUR 480 million of equity from Halden Group, EUR 130 million of equity from co-investors (currently anticipated to include two existing LP relationships), and EUR 540 million of senior and second-lien debt. Total leverage at close is approximately 5.2x trailing EBITDA, which we view as appropriate given the Company's cash generation profile and recession-resilient end-market mix. Goldman Sachs and Credit Suisse have provided fully underwritten commitments.

The Schiller family will retain a 15% economic interest. Management will hold the remaining 7%. We have negotiated standard tag-along and drag-along rights, and a clear governance framework giving Halden Group majority board representation (3 of 5 seats).
CLOSING CONSIDERATIONS

Diligence has been thorough. We engaged Bain & Company on commercial diligence (six weeks, completed late February), Deloitte on financial and tax diligence, Kirkland & Ellis on legal, and ERM on ESG and environmental diligence. The Bain report — circulated separately — confirms our market positioning thesis and identifies an additional EUR 14 million of revenue synergies from cross-selling between segments that we have not underwritten in the base case.

We have agreed exclusivity through 31 March 2025 and expect to sign definitive documentation by 28 March. Closing is targeted for mid-June, subject to merger control clearances in the EU, US, and Switzerland. No competition issues are anticipated.

HPC represents an attractive opportunity to acquire a category leader in a structurally growing market with a clear operational improvement plan and proven through-cycle resilience. The base case returns of 2.4x / 19% are in line with our private equity portfolio benchmarks, and we see meaningful upside optionality from M&A and end-market acceleration. The risks are well-understood and manageable. We recommend approval.

The leadership transition has proceeded smoothly, with Petra Köhler establishing herself well as CEO. Two material risks have emerged that we are actively managing: a slowdown in semiconductor capital equipment orders, and an unexpected quality issue at one medical device customer.

EBITDA of EUR 58 million versus a budget of EUR 54 million was driven by three factors: favourable mix (the strength in medical was higher-margin than budgeted), early procurement wins (Klaus Wenger has already secured EUR 2.1 million of annualised savings against a year-one target of EUR 5 million), and modest favourable FX (CHF weakened to 1.02 against EUR over the period, against our base case of 0.98).

For full-year 2025, we expect revenue of approximately EUR 625 million and EBITDA of approximately EUR 113 million, representing 6% revenue growth and 18.1% EBITDA margins on a full-year basis. This is broadly in line with our underwriting trajectory.

EBITDA of EUR 58 million was 7% above plan, with margins of 18.3% reflecting early traction on the procurement programme and favourable mix. The leadership transition has proceeded smoothly, with Petra Köhler establishing herself well as CEO. Two material risks have emerged that we are actively managing: a slowdown in semiconductor capital equipment orders, and an unexpected quality issue at one medical device customer.

The CEO transition has gone better than expected. Petra Köhler took over from Andreas Schiller on 16 June and has moved decisively on early priorities — restructuring the procurement function, initiating the Winterthur footprint review, and establishing a monthly operating cadence with the Halden Group team. Andreas Schiller has integrated comfortably into his board role and continues to provide useful customer-facing support.

Medical device customer quality issue: In October, our second-largest medical customer raised a quality concern relating to a specific component lot manufactured in the Olten facility. Initial root cause analysis points to a tooling wear issue that was not detected by in-process inspection. The cost impact to HPC is limited — approximately EUR 3 million in returns, rework, and credit — but the relationship cost is more significant. Petra Köhler met the customer's COO in November and the customer is satisfied with the corrective action plan. However the customer has placed HPC on enhanced quality monitoring for 12 months, which is an unwelcome development. We are tracking this closely.

The CEO transition has gone better than expected. Petra Köhler took over from Andreas Schiller on 16 June and has moved decisively on early priorities — restructuring the procurement function, initiating the Winterthur footprint review, and establishing a monthly operating cadence with the Halden Group team. Andreas Schiller has integrated comfortably into his board role and continues to provide useful customer-facing support.

Winterthur footprint review: Site closure is now under formal consultation with the workforce, with a target closure date of June 2026. Approximately 180 roles are affected; roughly 60 are expected to transfer to Olten. The associated restructuring charge of EUR 22 million has been provided in the period. We expect annualised savings of EUR 14 million from full transition, slightly above our underwriting estimate of EUR 12 million.

The next major milestones are: completion of the French add-on (Q1 2026), Brno automation phase one going live (Q3 2026), and Winterthur consolidation completion (mid-2026). We will provide a further detailed update at the 12-month review in June 2026.

occurrences.extract: PORTFOLIO COMPANY UPDATE — STRICTLY CONFIDENTIAL

Six months into our investment in HPC, performance is tracking modestly ahead of the base case underwritten at IC. Revenue for the period reached EUR 318 million, 4% above plan. EBITDA of EUR 58 million was 7% above plan, with margins of 18.3% reflecting early traction on the procurement programme and favourable mix. The leadership transition has proceeded smoothly, with Petra Köhler establishing herself well as CEO. Two material risks have emerged that we are actively managing: a slowdown in semiconductor capital equipment orders, and an unexpected quality issue at one medical device customer.

We have recruited two of the three new senior hires planned in our underwriting. Klaus Wenger joined as Chief Procurement Officer in September, having previously held the same role at Belimo. He brings strong category management discipline that the Company has historically lacked. Sophie Lehmann joined as Chief Commercial Officer in October from GF Machining Solutions. The remaining priority hire — a VP of Digital and Automation — is in late-stage interviews with two strong candidates; we expect this role to be filled by end-Q1 2026.

Period revenue of EUR 318 million represents growth of 11% versus the prior comparable period. The medical implants segment grew 14%, well ahead of expectations, driven by a 22% increase from our largest orthopaedic customer following their successful US product launch. Aerospace revenue grew 9%, broadly in line with build-rate increases at Airbus. Semiconductor revenue declined 6% in the period, reflecting weaker orders from two key customers (see Risks section below).

EBITDA of EUR 58 million versus a budget of EUR 54 million was driven by three factors: favourable mix (the strength in medical was higher-margin than budgeted), early procurement wins (Klaus Wenger has already secured EUR 2.1 million of annualised savings against a year-one target of EUR 5 million), and modest favourable FX (CHF weakened to 1.02 against EUR over the period, against our base case of 0.98).

Cash conversion was 68%, slightly below the 71% historical average, reflecting a planned working capital build to support the medical segment ramp. Net debt at period end stood at EUR 512 million, down EUR 28 million from close.

Procurement programme: Klaus Wenger has built a 90-day diagnostic. He has identified EUR 11 million of addressable savings across consolidation, demand management, and renegotiation — broadly in line with our diligence estimate. EUR 2.1 million is now contracted; he expects to be at a EUR 6 million annualised run-rate by mid-2026.

M&A pipeline: We have advanced two of the five targets identified pre-close. The first — a French specialist in titanium machining — is in second-round bids; we expect to know within six weeks whether we have been selected. The second — a German family business in optical components — has agreed to enter exclusivity in January 2026 at a preliminary valuation of EUR 42 million.

Semiconductor slowdown: We flagged this as a cyclical risk in our underwriting and the early signals are now visible. Two semiconductor capital equipment customers have pushed orders by one to two quarters. We do not expect a deep downturn — the demand picture for EUV remains structurally strong — but we are guiding to flat semiconductor revenue for the next 12 months and have adjusted our full-year forecast accordingly. The full-year 2026 budget assumes semiconductor revenue of EUR 105 million versus our original underwriting of EUR 122 million.

Medical device customer quality issue: In October, our second-largest medical customer raised a quality concern relating to a specific component lot manufactured in the Olten facility. Initial root cause analysis points to a tooling wear issue that was not detected by in-process inspection. The cost impact to HPC is limited — approximately EUR 3 million in returns, rework, and credit — but the relationship cost is more significant. Petra Köhler met the customer's COO in November and the customer is satisfied with the corrective action plan. However the customer has placed HPC on enhanced quality monitoring for 12 months, which is an unwelcome development. We are tracking this closely.

We remain confident in our base case returns of 2.4x MOIC and 19% IRR. The early traction on procurement and the strength in medical implants are partial offsets to the semiconductor weakness and the customer quality issue. We do not at this stage see reason to revise our underwriting.

occurrences.extract: There has been one departure of concern: Tom Beasley, who ran the Indianapolis operation, resigned in August to join a US competitor. We have backfilled the role with Mark Rivera, previously plant manager at the Olten facility, on a 12-month assignment. This is a reasonable interim solution but the US business will need a permanent leader by mid-2026.

Semiconductor slowdown: We flagged this as a cyclical risk in our underwriting and the early signals are now visible. Two semiconductor capital equipment customers have pushed orders by one to two quarters. We do not expect a deep downturn — the demand picture for EUV remains structurally strong — but we are guiding to flat semiconductor revenue for the next 12 months and have adjusted our full-year forecast accordingly. The full-year 2026 budget assumes semiconductor revenue of EUR 105 million versus our original underwriting of EUR 122 million.

occurrences.extract: We have recruited two of the three new senior hires planned in our underwriting. Klaus Wenger joined as Chief Procurement Officer in September, having previously held the same role at Belimo. He brings strong category management discipline that the Company has historically lacked. Sophie Lehmann joined as Chief Commercial Officer in October from GF Machining Solutions. The remaining priority hire — a VP of Digital and Automation — is in late-stage interviews with two strong candidates; we expect this role to be filled by end-Q1 2026.

EBITDA of EUR 58 million versus a budget of EUR 54 million was driven by three factors: favourable mix (the strength in medical was higher-margin than budgeted), early procurement wins (Klaus Wenger has already secured EUR 2.1 million of annualised savings against a year-one target of EUR 5 million), and modest favourable FX (CHF weakened to 1.02 against EUR over the period, against our base case of 0.98).

Procurement programme: Klaus Wenger has built a 90-day diagnostic. He has identified EUR 11 million of addressable savings across consolidation, demand management, and renegotiation — broadly in line with our diligence estimate. EUR 2.1 million is now contracted; he expects to be at a EUR 6 million annualised run-rate by mid-2026.

occurrences.extract: Meridian Capital completes acquisition of Lumen Specialty Chemicals

Frankfurt, Germany — 8 October 2025 — Meridian Capital ("Meridian"), the global private markets firm, today announced the successful completion of its acquisition of Lumen Specialty Chemicals GmbH ("Lumen" or "the Company"), a leading European producer of high-purity specialty chemicals for the electronics, pharmaceutical, and advanced materials industries. The transaction was first announced in June 2025.

"Lumen represents exactly the type of investment opportunity Meridian is built to pursue," said Henrik Vossberg, Partner and Head of European Industrials at Meridian Capital. "It is a category-leading business serving structurally growing end markets, with a strong management team and meaningful opportunities for operational improvement and international expansion. We are delighted to partner with the Lumen team on the next phase of growth."

The acquisition is the eighth investment from Meridian's flagship European Industrials strategy and brings the firm's total invested capital in the specialty chemicals sector to over EUR 2 billion across its global platforms.
About Meridian Capital

Meridian Capital is a global private markets firm with EUR 95 billion in assets under management. The firm invests in private equity, infrastructure, and private credit across Europe, North America, and Asia, on behalf of institutional and private wealth clients. Founded in 2002 and headquartered in Zurich, Meridian employs over 1,400 professionals across 14 offices worldwide.
Meridian Capital — Sarah Bauer, sarah.bauer@meridiancapital.example, +41 41 555 0100

occurrences.extract: Meridian Capital completes acquisition of Lumen Specialty Chemicals

Frankfurt, Germany — 8 October 2025 — Meridian Capital ("Meridian"), the global private markets firm, today announced the successful completion of its acquisition of Lumen Specialty Chemicals GmbH ("Lumen" or "the Company"), a leading European producer of high-purity specialty chemicals for the electronics, pharmaceutical, and advanced materials industries. The transaction was first announced in June 2025.

"Lumen represents exactly the type of investment opportunity Meridian is built to pursue," said Henrik Vossberg, Partner and Head of European Industrials at Meridian Capital. "It is a category-leading business serving structurally growing end markets, with a strong management team and meaningful opportunities for operational improvement and international expansion. We are delighted to partner with the Lumen team on the next phase of growth."

Lumen will be led by its existing Chief Executive Officer, Dr. Annika Brandt, who has held the role since 2019. The senior management team will remain in place. Meridian will support the Company's expansion strategy, with particular focus on the rapidly growing Asian electronics market and on selective acquisitions in adjacent specialty chemical categories.

"This is an important milestone for Lumen," said Dr. Annika Brandt, Chief Executive Officer of Lumen Specialty Chemicals. "Meridian brings deep expertise in our industry and a long-term perspective that aligns with our growth ambitions. Together we will accelerate our investment in capacity expansion, technology, and the talented people who make Lumen what it is."

The acquisition is the eighth investment from Meridian's flagship European Industrials strategy and brings the firm's total invested capital in the specialty chemicals sector to over EUR 2 billion across its global platforms.
Meridian was advised by Rothschild & Co (financial), Hengeler Mueller (legal), and Roland Berger (commercial). The seller was advised by Lazard.
About Meridian Capital

Meridian Capital is a global private markets firm with EUR 95 billion in assets under management. The firm invests in private equity, infrastructure, and private credit across Europe, North America, and Asia, on behalf of institutional and private wealth clients. Founded in 2002 and headquartered in Zurich, Meridian employs over 1,400 professionals across 14 offices worldwide.
Meridian Capital — Sarah Bauer, sarah.bauer@meridiancapital.example, +41 41 555 0100

occurrences.extract: Meridian Capital completes acquisition of Lumen Specialty Chemicals

Frankfurt, Germany — 8 October 2025 — Meridian Capital ("Meridian"), the global private markets firm, today announced the successful completion of its acquisition of Lumen Specialty Chemicals GmbH ("Lumen" or "the Company"), a leading European producer of high-purity specialty chemicals for the electronics, pharmaceutical, and advanced materials industries. The transaction was first announced in June 2025.

"Lumen represents exactly the type of investment opportunity Meridian is built to pursue," said Henrik Vossberg, Partner and Head of European Industrials at Meridian Capital. "It is a category-leading business serving structurally growing end markets, with a strong management team and meaningful opportunities for operational improvement and international expansion. We are delighted to partner with the Lumen team on the next phase of growth."

Lumen will be led by its existing Chief Executive Officer, Dr. Annika Brandt, who has held the role since 2019. The senior management team will remain in place. Meridian will support the Company's expansion strategy, with particular focus on the rapidly growing Asian electronics market and on selective acquisitions in adjacent specialty chemical categories.

"This is an important milestone for Lumen," said Dr. Annika Brandt, Chief Executive Officer of Lumen Specialty Chemicals. "Meridian brings deep expertise in our industry and a long-term perspective that aligns with our growth ambitions. Together we will accelerate our investment in capacity expansion, technology, and the talented people who make Lumen what it is."

The acquisition is the eighth investment from Meridian's flagship European Industrials strategy and brings the firm's total invested capital in the specialty chemicals sector to over EUR 2 billion across its global platforms.
Meridian was advised by Rothschild & Co (financial), Hengeler Mueller (legal), and Roland Berger (commercial). The seller was advised by Lazard.
About Meridian Capital

Meridian Capital is a global private markets firm with EUR 95 billion in assets under management. The firm invests in private equity, infrastructure, and private credit across Europe, North America, and Asia, on behalf of institutional and private wealth clients. Founded in 2002 and headquartered in Zurich, Meridian employs over 1,400 professionals across 14 offices worldwide.
Meridian Capital — Sarah Bauer, sarah.bauer@meridiancapital.example, +41 41 555 0100

occurrences.extract: After eighteen months of work alongside the team, I'm delighted that Meridian Capital has completed the sale of NorTech Industries to Brookfield this week. NorTech is a Stockholm-headquartered manufacturer of industrial heating and cooling systems, and one of those quiet category leaders that the Nordic region produces so well.

When we acquired NorTech in 2021 it was an excellent company with a clear ceiling — strong in Sweden, under-exposed everywhere else, and held back by a fragmented shareholder structure. Four and a half years later it is a genuinely international business with operations across the Nordic region, Germany, France, the UK, and Poland.
The wider NorTech team in Stockholm and across the new international footprint, who have built something exceptional.
Onwards. Excited to see what NorTech does next under Brookfield's ownership.

occurrences.extract: After eighteen months of work alongside the team, I'm delighted that Meridian Capital has completed the sale of NorTech Industries to Brookfield this week. NorTech is a Stockholm-headquartered manufacturer of industrial heating and cooling systems, and one of those quiet category leaders that the Nordic region produces so well.

When we acquired NorTech in 2021 it was an excellent company with a clear ceiling — strong in Sweden, under-exposed everywhere else, and held back by a fragmented shareholder structure. Four and a half years later it is a genuinely international business with operations across the Nordic region, Germany, France, the UK, and Poland.
The wider NorTech team in Stockholm and across the new international footprint, who have built something exceptional.
Onwards. Excited to see what NorTech does next under Brookfield's ownership.

occurrences.extract: Subject:   Project Borealis — Proposed acquisition of CloudPivot Systems Limited

We seek IC approval for an investment of EUR 285 million for a 64% controlling stake in CloudPivot Systems Limited ("CloudPivot" or "the Company"), a London-headquartered vertical SaaS platform serving the European logistics and freight forwarding industry. The transaction values CloudPivot at an enterprise value of EUR 445 million. On a trailing basis the Company generates an EBITDA margin of approximately 13%, reflecting continued investment in product and go-to-market.

Vertical SaaS economics. Freight forwarding is a deeply specialised industry with workflow patterns that horizontal ERP systems handle poorly. CloudPivot's product reflects ten years of domain investment and is genuinely differentiated. The closest international comparable, US-focused CargoOne, was acquired by Thoma Bravo in early 2024 at 11x ARR.

Mission-critical software with very low churn. Once a forwarder is operating on CloudPivot, switching costs are very high. The platform integrates with customs authorities, carrier networks, and customer systems; reverting to alternative software would mean rebuilding all of these integrations. Gross retention of 94% reflects this.

occurrences.extract: We seek IC approval for an investment of EUR 285 million for a 64% controlling stake in CloudPivot Systems Limited ("CloudPivot" or "the Company"), a London-headquartered vertical SaaS platform serving the European logistics and freight forwarding industry. The transaction values CloudPivot at an enterprise value of EUR 445 million. On a trailing basis the Company generates an EBITDA margin of approximately 13%, reflecting continued investment in product and go-to-market.

CloudPivot was founded in London in 2014 by Tom Fairfield (currently CEO) and James O'Brien (currently CTO). The Company provides a comprehensive SaaS platform for freight forwarders and customs brokers, replacing the legacy ERP-style software that dominates the industry. The platform handles shipment booking, customs documentation, rate management, invoicing, and customer portal functionality through a single integrated product.

The Company serves over 1,200 freight forwarder and customs broker customers across 28 European countries. Customers range from single-office operators with 5 to 10 users up to mid-sized regional networks with 200+ users. CloudPivot has not yet meaningfully penetrated the largest global forwarders (Kuehne+Nagel, DHL, DB Schenker, DSV), although a recent pilot with DSV's Italian subsidiary has produced encouraging results.
The Company has been free cash flow positive since 2023. Cash on balance sheet at September 2025 stood at EUR 18 million with no debt.

ARR growth from EUR 81 million today to approximately EUR 195 million over a five-year hold. This represents 19% CAGR, reflecting a measured deceleration from the recent 27% pace as the Company scales.

CloudPivot generates annual recurring revenue ("ARR") of EUR 84 million as of October 2025, up from EUR 52 million two years prior — representing 27% CAGR. Net revenue retention has averaged 113% over the past 24 months, with gross retention of 94%. Customer acquisition cost payback is 14 months, broadly in line with vertical SaaS benchmarks.

CloudPivot is a high-quality vertical SaaS asset with strong unit economics, a defensible competitive position, and a clear growth runway. We have strong conviction in the founders and the team. We recommend approval.

occurrences.extract: We seek IC approval for an investment of EUR 285 million for a 64% controlling stake in CloudPivot Systems Limited ("CloudPivot" or "the Company"), a London-headquartered vertical SaaS platform serving the European logistics and freight forwarding industry. The transaction values CloudPivot at an enterprise value of EUR 445 million. CloudPivot has not yet meaningfully penetrated the largest global forwarders (Kuehne+Nagel, DHL, DB Schenker, DSV), although a recent pilot with DSV's Italian subsidiary has produced encouraging results.

Large addressable market with limited modern competition. There are approximately 14,000 freight forwarders and customs brokers in Europe. CloudPivot serves 1,200 of these — an 8.6% penetration rate. The principal competition is fragmented legacy software (Riege, CargoWise — which is the dominant player in larger forwarders — and a long tail of regional incumbents). Most legacy products are visibly aged and customer satisfaction is consistently low.

Founder-led with deep industry credibility. Tom Fairfield came from the industry — he ran technology at a mid-sized UK forwarder before founding CloudPivot — and has built a deeply respected position in the European logistics technology community.

The senior team is strong. Tom Fairfield, CEO, and James O'Brien, CTO, are the co-founders and remain deeply engaged. Maria Santangelo, CRO, joined from HubSpot in 2022 and has rebuilt the European sales organisation. The CFO, Patrick Lawrence, joined from a private equity-backed UK SaaS business in 2024 and has tightened reporting and unit economics discipline.

The total team of 285 people is split approximately as follows: engineering 110, customer success and implementation 75, sales 55, customer support 35, and general & administrative 10. We see opportunities to invest further in product and in mid-market sales capacity in continental Europe.

Founder-led with deep industry credibility. Tom Fairfield came from the industry — he ran technology at a mid-sized UK forwarder before founding CloudPivot — and has built a deeply respected position in the European logistics technology community.

The senior team is strong. Tom Fairfield, CEO, and James O'Brien, CTO, are the co-founders and remain deeply engaged. Maria Santangelo, CRO, joined from HubSpot in 2022 and has rebuilt the European sales organisation. The CFO, Patrick Lawrence, joined from a private equity-backed UK SaaS business in 2024 and has tightened reporting and unit economics discipline.

The total team of 285 people is split approximately as follows: engineering 110, customer success and implementation 75, sales 55, customer support 35, and general & administrative 10. We see opportunities to invest further in product and in mid-market sales capacity in continental Europe.

Net revenue retention has averaged 113% over the past 24 months, with gross retention of 94%. Customer acquisition cost payback is 14 months, broadly in line with vertical SaaS benchmarks.

Vertical SaaS economics. Freight forwarding is a deeply specialised industry with workflow patterns that horizontal ERP systems handle poorly. CloudPivot's product reflects ten years of domain investment and is genuinely differentiated. The closest international comparable, US-focused CargoOne, was acquired by Thoma Bravo in early 2024 at 11x ARR.

Mission-critical software with very low churn. Once a forwarder is operating on CloudPivot, switching costs are very high. The platform integrates with customs authorities, carrier networks, and customer systems; reverting to alternative software would mean rebuilding all of these integrations. Gross retention of 94% reflects this.

occurrences.extract: CloudPivot was founded in London in 2014 by Tom Fairfield (currently CEO) and James O'Brien (currently CTO). The Company provides a comprehensive SaaS platform for freight forwarders and customs brokers, replacing the legacy ERP-style software that dominates the industry. The platform handles shipment booking, customs documentation, rate management, invoicing, and customer portal functionality through a single integrated product.

Founder-led with deep industry credibility. Tom Fairfield came from the industry — he ran technology at a mid-sized UK forwarder before founding CloudPivot — and has built a deeply respected position in the European logistics technology community.

Founder transition. CEO Tom Fairfield is 51 and has indicated willingness to remain for the duration of our hold. Should he wish to step back, we have identified the Chief Revenue Officer, Maria Santangelo, as a credible internal successor.

The senior team is strong. Tom Fairfield, CEO, and James O'Brien, CTO, are the co-founders and remain deeply engaged. Maria Santangelo, CRO, joined from HubSpot in 2022 and has rebuilt the European sales organisation. The CFO, Patrick Lawrence, joined from a private equity-backed UK SaaS business in 2024 and has tightened reporting and unit economics discipline.

We will invest EUR 285 million for 64% of the equity. The founders and management will retain 28% in aggregate (Tom Fairfield 14%, James O'Brien 7%, other management 7%) and existing growth equity investor Index Ventures will retain 8%. There is no third-party debt at close. We have negotiated standard governance with majority Halden Group board control (3 of 5 seats).

The Company has been free cash flow positive since 2023. Cash on balance sheet at September 2025 stood at EUR 18 million with no debt.

occurrences.extract: We seek IC approval for an investment of EUR 285 million for a 64% controlling stake in CloudPivot Systems Limited ("CloudPivot" or "the Company"), a London-headquartered vertical SaaS platform serving the European logistics and freight forwarding industry. The transaction values CloudPivot at an enterprise value of EUR 445 million. On a trailing basis the Company generates an EBITDA margin of approximately 13%, reflecting continued investment in product and go-to-market.

The Company serves over 1,200 freight forwarder and customs broker customers across 28 European countries. Customers range from single-office operators with 5 to 10 users up to mid-sized regional networks with 200+ users. CloudPivot has not yet meaningfully penetrated the largest global forwarders (Kuehne+Nagel, DHL, DB Schenker, DSV), although a recent pilot with DSV's Italian subsidiary has produced encouraging results.

Large addressable market with limited modern competition. There are approximately 14,000 freight forwarders and customs brokers in Europe. CloudPivot serves 1,200 of these — an 8.6% penetration rate. The principal competition is fragmented legacy software (Riege, CargoWise — which is the dominant player in larger forwarders — and a long tail of regional incumbents). Most legacy products are visibly aged and customer satisfaction is consistently low.

Founder-led with deep industry credibility. Tom Fairfield came from the industry — he ran technology at a mid-sized UK forwarder before founding CloudPivot — and has built a deeply respected position in the European logistics technology community.

The senior team is strong. Tom Fairfield, CEO, and James O'Brien, CTO, are the co-founders and remain deeply engaged. Maria Santangelo, CRO, joined from HubSpot in 2022 and has rebuilt the European sales organisation. The CFO, Patrick Lawrence, joined from a private equity-backed UK SaaS business in 2024 and has tightened reporting and unit economics discipline.

The total team of 285 people is split approximately as follows: engineering 110, customer success and implementation 75, sales 55, customer support 35, and general & administrative 10. We see opportunities to invest further in product and in mid-market sales capacity in continental Europe.

Net revenue retention has averaged 113% over the past 24 months, with gross retention of 94%. Customer acquisition cost payback is 14 months, broadly in line with vertical SaaS benchmarks.

Mission-critical software with very low churn. Once a forwarder is operating on CloudPivot, switching costs are very high. The transaction values CloudPivot at an enterprise value of EUR 445 million. On a trailing basis the Company generates an EBITDA margin of approximately 13%, reflecting continued investment in product and go-to-market.

CloudPivot was founded in London in 2014 by Tom Fairfield (currently CEO) and James O'Brien (currently CTO). The Company provides a comprehensive SaaS platform for freight forwarders and customs brokers, replacing the legacy ERP-style software that dominates the industry. The platform handles shipment booking, customs documentation, rate management, invoicing, and customer portal functionality through a single integrated product.

Customers range from single-office operators with 5 to 10 users up to mid-sized regional networks with 200+ users. CloudPivot has not yet meaningfully penetrated the largest global forwarders (Kuehne+Nagel, DHL, DB Schenker, DSV), although a recent pilot with DSV's Italian subsidiary has produced encouraging results.
The Company has been free cash flow positive since 2023. Cash on balance sheet at September 2025 stood at EUR 18 million with no debt.

occurrences.extract: Subject:   Investment thesis — European clinical decision support software

This memo sets out a thematic investment thesis on European clinical decision support ("CDS") software. It is not a transaction memo. We are not yet in dialogue with any specific company. The purpose is to seek Committee endorsement of the thesis itself, which would authorise the team to begin active sourcing and to engage with potential targets at the appropriate level.

The European CDS market is structurally distinct from the US market in several ways. European healthcare is dominated by national payers, which gives CDS products a clearer route to scale once adopted by a national authority. Reimbursement codes for digital health products have improved meaningfully across the major European markets over the past three years. Medical Device Regulation has created higher barriers to entry for serious clinical software, advantaging incumbents who have invested in the regulatory pathway.

We believe the European market is at an inflection point. Three forces are aligning. First, the regulatory pathway under EU MDR is now well-understood and incumbents have built up significant clearances. Second, payer willingness to reimburse CDS software has improved markedly. Third, generative AI is creating both opportunity and pressure: opportunity to genuinely improve clinical workflows, pressure on incumbents who lack credible AI strategies.
The thesis fits our European healthcare investment platform well.

The European competitive landscape is fragmented across national markets. National scale leaders exist in the UK, Germany, France, and the Nordics, but few players have meaningful pan-European presence. This creates the conditions for a buy-and-build strategy that pairs well with our M&A capabilities.

The category has been under-served by private equity to date. Most scaled European CDS businesses are either bootstrapped, owned by clinical professional bodies, or sit inside larger health IT groups. There is meaningful opportunity for a thoughtful financial sponsor to play a constructive consolidation role.

We see the ideal target as having most of the following characteristics: leadership in at least one national European market; clinical credibility evidenced by professional society endorsement or integration into national clinical guidelines; recurring revenue base of at least EUR 25 million with growth above 15% annually; gross retention above 90%; demonstrated regulatory infrastructure under EU MDR; and a management team genuinely engaged with the AI shift rather than defensive about it.

What is the realistic path to pan-European scale given the inherent fragmentation of European healthcare? Is true cross-border integration achievable, or is the realistic model a portfolio of national champions under common ownership?

European clinical decision support is a structurally attractive software category at an inflection point. We believe it fits our platform well and we recommend Committee endorsement of active sourcing.

occurrences.extract: Subject:   Investment thesis — European clinical decision support software

This memo sets out a thematic investment thesis on European clinical decision support ("CDS") software. It is not a transaction memo. We are not yet in dialogue with any specific company. The purpose is to seek Committee endorsement of the thesis itself, which would authorise the team to begin active sourcing and to engage with potential targets at the appropriate level.

The European CDS market is structurally distinct from the US market in several ways. European healthcare is dominated by national payers, which gives CDS products a clearer route to scale once adopted by a national authority. Reimbursement codes for digital health products have improved meaningfully across the major European markets over the past three years. Medical Device Regulation has created higher barriers to entry for serious clinical software, advantaging incumbents who have invested in the regulatory pathway.

We believe the European market is at an inflection point. Three forces are aligning. First, the regulatory pathway under EU MDR is now well-understood and incumbents have built up significant clearances. Second, payer willingness to reimburse CDS software has improved markedly. Third, generative AI is creating both opportunity and pressure: opportunity to genuinely improve clinical workflows, pressure on incumbents who lack credible AI strategies.
The thesis fits our European healthcare investment platform well.

The European competitive landscape is fragmented across national markets. National scale leaders exist in the UK, Germany, France, and the Nordics, but few players have meaningful pan-European presence. This creates the conditions for a buy-and-build strategy that pairs well with our M&A capabilities.

The category has been under-served by private equity to date. Most scaled European CDS businesses are either bootstrapped, owned by clinical professional bodies, or sit inside larger health IT groups. There is meaningful opportunity for a thoughtful financial sponsor to play a constructive consolidation role.

We see the ideal target as having most of the following characteristics: leadership in at least one national European market; clinical credibility evidenced by professional society endorsement or integration into national clinical guidelines; recurring revenue base of at least EUR 25 million with growth above 15% annually; gross retention above 90%; demonstrated regulatory infrastructure under EU MDR; and a management team genuinely engaged with the AI shift rather than defensive about it.

What is the realistic path to pan-European scale given the inherent fragmentation of European healthcare? Is true cross-border integration achievable, or is the realistic model a portfolio of national champions under common ownership?

European clinical decision support is a structurally attractive software category at an inflection point. We believe it fits our platform well and we recommend Committee endorsement of active sourcing.

occurrences.extract: Clinical decision support software helps clinicians make better, faster, more consistent treatment decisions at the point of care. The category spans drug interaction checking, diagnostic decision trees, treatment protocol guidance, dosing calculators, and increasingly AI-augmented diagnostic assistance.

We believe the European market is at an inflection point. Three forces are aligning. First, the regulatory pathway under EU MDR is now well-understood and incumbents have built up significant clearances. Second, payer willingness to reimburse CDS software has improved markedly. Third, generative AI is creating both opportunity and pressure: opportunity to genuinely improve clinical workflows, pressure on incumbents who lack credible AI strategies.

The European competitive landscape is fragmented across national markets. National scale leaders exist in the UK, Germany, France, and the Nordics, but few players have meaningful pan-European presence. This creates the conditions for a buy-and-build strategy that pairs well with our M&A capabilities.

We see the ideal target as having most of the following characteristics: leadership in at least one national European market; clinical credibility evidenced by professional society endorsement or integration into national clinical guidelines; recurring revenue base of at least EUR 25 million with growth above 15% annually; gross retention above 90%; demonstrated regulatory infrastructure under EU MDR; and a management team genuinely engaged with the AI shift rather than defensive about it.

We would expect to invest at the platform level with a clear add-on programme. Typical deal size would be in the EUR 100 to 300 million equity ticket range, with an expected hold of five to seven years and a buy-and-build that aims to triple ARR over the hold.

What is the right competitive response to generative AI from a CDS business that has not yet built native AI capability? Is the answer to acquire AI-native challengers, to partner with foundation model providers, or to invest in proprietary models?

occurrences.extract: Subject:   Investment thesis — European clinical decision support software

This memo sets out a thematic investment thesis on European clinical decision support ("CDS") software. It is not a transaction memo. We are not yet in dialogue with any specific company. The purpose is to seek Committee endorsement of the thesis itself, which would authorise the team to begin active sourcing and to engage with potential targets at the appropriate level.

The European CDS market is structurally distinct from the US market in several ways. European healthcare is dominated by national payers, which gives CDS products a clearer route to scale once adopted by a national authority. Reimbursement codes for digital health products have improved meaningfully across the major European markets over the past three years. Medical Device Regulation has created higher barriers to entry for serious clinical software, advantaging incumbents who have invested in the regulatory pathway.

We believe the European market is at an inflection point. Three forces are aligning. First, the regulatory pathway under EU MDR is now well-understood and incumbents have built up significant clearances. Second, payer willingness to reimburse CDS software has improved markedly. Third, generative AI is creating both opportunity and pressure: opportunity to genuinely improve clinical workflows, pressure on incumbents who lack credible AI strategies.
The thesis fits our European healthcare investment platform well.

The European competitive landscape is fragmented across national markets. National scale leaders exist in the UK, Germany, France, and the Nordics, but few players have meaningful pan-European presence. This creates the conditions for a buy-and-build strategy that pairs well with our M&A capabilities.

The category has been under-served by private equity to date. Most scaled European CDS businesses are either bootstrapped, owned by clinical professional bodies, or sit inside larger health IT groups. There is meaningful opportunity for a thoughtful financial sponsor to play a constructive consolidation role.

We see the ideal target as having most of the following characteristics: leadership in at least one national European market; clinical credibility evidenced by professional society endorsement or integration into national clinical guidelines; recurring revenue base of at least EUR 25 million with growth above 15% annually; gross retention above 90%; demonstrated regulatory infrastructure under EU MDR; and a management team genuinely engaged with the AI shift rather than defensive about it.

What is the realistic path to pan-European scale given the inherent fragmentation of European healthcare? Is true cross-border integration achievable, or is the realistic model a portfolio of national champions under common ownership?

European clinical decision support is a structurally attractive software category at an inflection point. We believe it fits our platform well and we recommend Committee endorsement of active sourcing.

WHY THIS IS ATTRACTIVE FOR US

The category produces businesses with strong recurring revenue characteristics, mission-critical product positioning, and high regulatory barriers. Gross retention of 95%+ is typical. EBITDA margins for scaled players can exceed 30%.

The category has been under-served by private equity to date. Most scaled European CDS businesses are either bootstrapped, owned by clinical professional bodies, or sit inside larger health IT groups. There is meaningful opportunity for a thoughtful financial sponsor to play a constructive consolidation role.

What is the right competitive response to generative AI from a CDS business that has not yet built native AI capability? Is the answer to acquire AI-native challengers, to partner with foundation model providers, or to invest in proprietary models?

How should we think about the role of national health authorities as potential customers, partners, or competitors? In several markets there is active discussion of state-developed clinical decision tools.
CONCLUSION

From:      Healthcare Team — Anya Petrov (Member of Management), Felix Mertens (Senior Vice President)
Date:      18 September 2025
Subject:   Investment thesis — European clinical decision support software
PURPOSE OF THIS MEMO

This memo sets out a thematic investment thesis on European clinical decision support ("CDS") software. It is not a transaction memo. We are not yet in dialogue with any specific company. The purpose is to seek Committee endorsement of the thesis itself, which would authorise the team to begin active sourcing and to engage with potential targets at the appropriate level.

Clinical decision support software helps clinicians make better, faster, more consistent treatment decisions at the point of care. The category spans drug interaction checking, diagnostic decision trees, treatment protocol guidance, dosing calculators, and increasingly AI-augmented diagnostic assistance.

The European CDS market is structurally distinct from the US market in several ways. European healthcare is dominated by national payers, which gives CDS products a clearer route to scale once adopted by a national authority. Reimbursement codes for digital health products have improved meaningfully across the major European markets over the past three years. Medical Device Regulation has created higher barriers to entry for serious clinical software, advantaging incumbents who have invested in the regulatory pathway.

We believe the European market is at an inflection point. Three forces are aligning. First, the regulatory pathway under EU MDR is now well-understood and incumbents have built up significant clearances. Second, payer willingness to reimburse CDS software has improved markedly. Third, generative AI is creating both opportunity and pressure: opportunity to genuinely improve clinical workflows, pressure on incumbents who lack credible AI strategies.
The thesis fits our European healthcare investment platform well.

The category produces businesses with strong recurring revenue characteristics, mission-critical product positioning, and high regulatory barriers. Gross retention of 95%+ is typical. EBITDA margins for scaled players can exceed 30%.

The European competitive landscape is fragmented across national markets. National scale leaders exist in the UK, Germany, France, and the Nordics, but few players have meaningful pan-European presence. This creates the conditions for a buy-and-build strategy that pairs well with our M&A capabilities.

The category has been under-served by private equity to date. Most scaled European CDS businesses are either bootstrapped, owned by clinical professional bodies, or sit inside larger health IT groups. There is meaningful opportunity for a thoughtful financial sponsor to play a constructive consolidation role.

We see the ideal target as having most of the following characteristics: leadership in at least one national European market; clinical credibility evidenced by professional society endorsement or integration into national clinical guidelines; recurring revenue base of at least EUR 25 million with growth above 15% annually; gross retention above 90%; demonstrated regulatory infrastructure under EU MDR; and a management team genuinely engaged with the AI shift rather than defensive about it.

We would expect to invest at the platform level with a clear add-on programme. Typical deal size would be in the EUR 100 to 300 million equity ticket range, with an expected hold of five to seven years and a buy-and-build that aims to triple ARR over the hold.
If the Committee endorses this thesis we propose to:

Conduct a structured market mapping exercise over the next eight weeks, working with a specialist healthcare technology advisor. We have approached Mariner Health (a London-based boutique) for an initial scoping conversation.
Begin proactive outreach to a shortlist of approximately 15 to 20 potential targets identified through our preliminary work.

Engage clinical advisors to support our diligence approach on individual opportunities. We have had preliminary conversations with two former chief clinical officers of major UK and German hospital networks.
Plan to return to the Committee within six months with either a specific transaction memo or a refreshed thesis based on what we have learned.
We are not recommending any specific investment at this time. We are seeking endorsement of the thesis and authorisation to invest sourcing time accordingly.

What is the right competitive response to generative AI from a CDS business that has not yet built native AI capability? Is the answer to acquire AI-native challengers, to partner with foundation model providers, or to invest in proprietary models?

How should we think about the role of national health authorities as potential customers, partners, or competitors? In several markets there is active discussion of state-developed clinical decision tools.

What is the realistic path to pan-European scale given the inherent fragmentation of European healthcare? Is true cross-border integration achievable, or is the realistic model a portfolio of national champions under common ownership?
These questions will be sharpened through the sourcing and market mapping work. We would expect to return with clearer perspectives in the next thesis update.

European clinical decision support is a structurally attractive software category at an inflection point. We believe it fits our platform well and we recommend Committee endorsement of active sourcing.

occurrences.extract: Subject:   Project Tabula — Proposed acquisition of Casa Verde Group S.p.A.

We seek IC approval for an investment of up to EUR 720 million of equity in the acquisition of Casa Verde Group S.p.A. ("Casa Verde" or "the Company"), a Milan-headquartered premium European homeware and kitchenware retailer and brand owner. The transaction values Casa Verde at an enterprise value of EUR 1.85 billion, representing 12.4x trailing twelve months EBITDA of EUR 149 million.

Casa Verde was founded in 1973 by Giovanni Esposito as a single homewares shop in Milan. The Company has grown organically and through measured acquisitions into a pan-European premium homeware and kitchenware specialist with operations across Italy, France, Spain, and Germany. The Company currently operates 184 retail stores, an e-commerce platform that generates 31% of group revenue, and a wholesale business that supplies independent design-led homeware retailers across Europe.

We recommend approval of an investment of up to EUR 720 million of equity from Halden Group, with the right to syndicate up to EUR 110 million of co-investment, in the acquisition of Casa Verde Group S.p.A. on the terms described.
